Duration::total().weeks()¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

DurationTotal Duration::total() const;
Series DurationTotal::weeks() const;

What It Does¶

Converts a Duration’s elapsed magnitude into a plain Series expressed in weeks — total().nanoseconds() divided by 7 * 86'400 * 1e9. The coarsest unit accessor in this family. See total().nanoseconds() for the full explanation of the total() accessor.

Parameters¶

None — this is a zero-argument accessor on self.

Returns¶

Series A floating-point Series at self’s shape, in weeks.

Examples¶

Example 1. A 21-day Duration read as weeks.

auto three_weeks = pluss::duration::days(21);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(three_weeks.total().weeks());

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=3.0000

21 days is exactly 3 weeks.

Notes¶

  • .total().weeks() never rounds or truncates — a duration that isn’t an exact multiple of a week reads back as a non-integer number of weeks, same as every other unit accessor in this family.

See Also¶

  • total().days(): the finer unit this divides.

  • total().nanoseconds(): the finest unit, and the value every accessor in this family is ultimately derived from.
